content_html:
Peru is a paradise for trekking lovers. Its mountainous landscapes, deep valleys, crystalline lagoons and archaeological sites make each route a unique experience. If you are an adventurer in search of challenges and unforgettable landscapes, here we present you the 5 best trekking in Peru that you can't miss.

1. Inca Trail: The Classic Route to Machu Picchu

Location: Cusco
Duration: 4 days / 3 nights
Difficulty: Medium – High

The Inca Trail It is the most famous trekking in Peru and one of the most iconic in the world. This 42 km ancient route passes through impressive Andean landscapes, cloud forests and hidden archaeological sites, until reaching the majestic citadel of Machu Picchu. The great reward is to cross the Gate of the Sun (Inti Punku) at dawn and see the sacred city illuminated by the first rays of the sun.

Tip: Book months in advance, since access is limited to 500 people per day.

2. Trekking to Laguna 69: Heavenly Beauty in Huaraz

Location: Huascarán National Park, Áncash
Duration: 1 day
Difficulty: Medium – High

If you are looking for a short but challenging trek, the hike to Lagoon 69 It is one of the best options. Located at 4,600 meters above sea level, this turquoise blue lagoon is surrounded by imposing snow-capped mountains such as Huascarán and Chacraraju. The final climb is demanding, but the panoramic view makes every step worth it.

Tip: Acclimatize for at least one day in Huaraz before trekking to avoid altitude sickness.

3. Trekking to the Colca Canyon: Between Condors and Depths

Location: Arequipa
Duration: 2 to 3 days
Difficulty: Medium – High

The Colca Canyon, one of the deepest in the world (3,270 m), is the perfect setting for an epic hike. The route includes impressive views of the canyon, natural viewpoints to spot the andean condor, and descents to hidden oases such as Sangalle, where you can enjoy hot springs.

Tip: Get ready for the final climb of more than 1,000 meters; It is the most demanding challenge of trekking.

4. Trekking to the Mountain of 7 Colors: Vinicunca at its Maximum Expression

Location: Cusco
Duration: 1 day
Difficulty: Medium – High

The Mountain of 7 Colors (Vinicunca) It has become a must-see destination for nature lovers. Your trekking of approx. 4km (one way) takes you to 5,200 meters above sea level, where you will witness a multicolored landscape unique in the world.

Tip: Start your hike early to avoid crowds and bad weather. You can also opt for the Palccoyo Mountain, which is less demanding and less crowded.

5. Trekking to Nevado Ausangate and its Seven Lagoons

Location: Cusco
Duration: 5 to 6 days (full) / 1 day (Siete Lagunas)
Difficulty: High

For the more experienced adventurers, the Trekking to Nevado Ausangate It is one of the most impressive and challenging routes in Peru. During the tour, you cross high mountain landscapes, glaciers, hot springs and lagoons of different colors. If you don't have that much time, a shorter option is the day hike to Seven Lagoons of Ausangate.

Tip: This trekking requires a good acclimatization due to the extreme altitude.
